why: The two sides reach DIFFERENT N/A branches, and the first is what keeps this rule from burning the tool. Measured on 2026-08-30: ignoring the applicability gate, the definition of a content literal finds 188 occurrences across the 11 repositories — 185 sentences and 3 prices; and 17 of them are fragments, not literals, because the match cuts at the first `<` — 147 in `decima-edicoes` alone, in 15 of its 25 files. None is false, and that is precisely the problem: EVERY hand-written site violates the assertion, so it can only be charged to whoever promised to keep it. The `pass` side has a price AND a sentence planted in the `.tsx` and does NOT have `conteudo/`, and has to come out N/A — whoever removes the gate turns this side red and the rule starts accusing half the world. The `fail` side has `conteudo/` and no code in `src/` or in `app/`: a promise with no object is not evaluated either.
